posts.name: JimmytheRat
posts.cooked:
Fixer is also interesting in that he can destroy ongoings only when he's incapacitated.  Having Fixer go down first has saved me against Iron Legacy before.

I do think that incap abilities are supposed to be strong to help get your team back in the game, and to balance the fact that you can only do one thing a turn.  There's a 2-hero variant with H=3, two live heroes and one incapacitated hero at the start of the game, and I've found it to be actually stronger than regular H=3 half the time.  Unless you've got a villain/environment that gangs up on the lowest HP target a lot, most of your team is likely in the single digits by the time the incap abilities become available normally.  Getting them at the beginning of the game can potentially be just downright silly.

I don't mean to say that incap abilities can't come in very handy in certain situations, nor that you've got the rules wrong, but it would be helpful to clarify any such encounters.

oh so the damage has to come from a source to be negated? Would that include environmental targets like dinosaurs and other enemies? Or are they excluded as well?

Grease Gun stops damage coming from targets, so its not blocking damage coming from all sources, just sources that are targets.
